conviction_note: The one genuinely unpriced thing I found - a first-in-six-years increase to SAIC's government-receivables sale facility, signed two weeks after the quarter it cannot help - is real and uncovered, but its sign is ambiguous between 'Q2 working capital deteriorated' and 'management is arming a liquidity lever for buybacks/M&A', and its more probable bearish reading merely agrees with a skew already paying 6.9 vol points for downside, so it does not structurally earn a call against a 9.4% implied move.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-14 SAIC raised its MUFG Master Accounts Receivable Purchase facility from $300M to $400M - the first size increase since March 2020 and only the third time in six years it has filed an 8-K Item 1.01 on this facility - signed two weeks after fiscal Q2 closed on 31 July, so the extra capacity cannot touch the quarter being reported; at the last balance sheet date receivables had risen from $853M to $962M (+12.8%) in one quarter on roughly flat revenue, cash had fallen from $182M to $109M, and only $164M of the $300M cap was in use.
findings.why_not_priced: SAIC's own non-GAAP definition explicitly subtracts MARPA cash flows from free cash flow (Q1 FY27 release, Schedule 6 note), so an expanded facility does nothing for the headline metric the stock is judged on - which is precisely why no sell-side note or wire story treats it as an earnings input. The only pickup was automated 8-K scrapers (StockTitan, TipRanks, TradingView) restating the headline number with no link to the receivables build. If this were priced, the 25-delta skew would not need to be the market's only directional statement: there would be a preview note on H1 cash conversion, and the stock would not be sitting 2.3% off its 52-week high after a +7.5% 20-day run-up. The tell that the market is reading SAIC purely off the February guidance reset and the August award press releases is that the run-up and the coverage are both entirely bookings-driven, with nothing on the balance sheet.
findings.independence: The Q1 FY27 10-Q corroborates the working-capital direction from a different document: receivables +$109M QoQ, cash -$73M, $203M SilverEdge acquisition funded from increased borrowings, and $201M of financing outflows including buybacks at $90-95/share - a balance sheet run deliberately tight. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571123/000157112326000079/saic-20260501.htm

searched_and_found_nothing: USAspending prime-obligation series for SAIC showed an apparent collapse from $525M in May 2026 to $195M in June and $203M in July - but I ran the identical query for Leidos ($693M/$414M/$258M) and CACI ($388M/$123M/$189M) and the shape reproduces exactly, so it is FPDS reporting lag, not a SAIC-specific demand signal. Killed my own best idea. (https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_over_time/)
Insider activity: only routine June 2026 director/officer equity grants and a July 6 Form 4 in the whole window - no sale cluster, no unusual 10b5-1 starts (SEC submissions API, CIK 0001571123)

GAO bid protest docket for protests filed BY SAIC in the May-July quarter, which would reveal recompete losses the company never press-released - gao.gov search endpoint returns Access Denied and I could not reconstruct it from secondary sources

Known recompete losses (CASTLE-NET/RITS to Accenture, GAO denial 2026-05-19; Cloud One) are the documented basis of the February FY27 guidance cut and are covered by Washington Technology - fully in the wire copy

August contract wins ($400M intel recompete 08-05, $232M Army, $118M VA 08-06, '$1.6B intel space in H1 FY27') are all company press releases carried by GlobeNewswire and the trades - priced, and mostly Q3 events anyway

Board expansion 10 to 12 with Benson (ex-Fannie Mae President/CFO) and Cush (ex-Virgin America CEO) on 2026-08-10 looked like an activist settlement shape, but it was press-released, widely covered, and carries no cooperation agreement or 13D - no activist found
CEO transition (Reagan interim October 2025, permanent February 2026) - thoroughly covered, not an edge
WARN notices and layoffs: nothing filed for SAIC in 2026; the five-groups-to-three reorganisation was disclosed in the 10-Q and the Attili departure in a 5.02 8-K on 06-01
FY2027 appropriations / October shutdown risk: Senate leaders reported a deal funding past the midterms to December 11 - macro and public
Q1 FY27 10-Q Item 1A states no material changes from the 10-K risk factors, so no filing-language shift to trade on
baseline_tension: My single finding's more likely reading points the same way as the +6.86 vol-point skew and therefore adds nothing the market has not already paid for, while nothing I found cuts against the +7.5% 20-day run-up into the 52-week high - which is exactly the configuration in which the honest answer is to stand aside rather than manufacture the contrarian half.
